memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So the sons of Israel did this. Joseph gave them carts, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he also gave them provisions for their journey. To each of them he gave new clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes." — Gen 45:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
New clothes for everyone. And for Benjamin — three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothing.

Some readers wince at this. Is Joseph repeating his father's mistake, favouring one son and stirring up the old jealousy all over again? Perhaps he is testing them one last time. But there may be something gentler here. Joseph is giving silver and a special robe — the very two things that were involved in his own betrayal. Silver was what they took for him. A robe was what they stripped from him. Now he hands both, freely, to the brother who might have been envied.

Whatever his exact motive, the brothers do not react as they once did. There is no muttering, no resentment. The old poison is gone. The clearest sign of a changed heart is being able to watch someone else receive more than you and feel no bitterness at all.

Test yourself here, gently. When someone else is blessed, promoted, praised, given what you wanted — what rises in you? That reaction tells you more about your heart than almost anything else.

Love, Paul says, does not envy (1 Cor 13:4). That kind of love is not manufactured by effort; it grows in a heart the Spirit has been working on for years, as He had been working on these men.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you react when someone else receives more than you?
2. Where has God freed you from envy you used to carry?
3. Who could you celebrate this week instead of quietly comparing yourself to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, search my heart for envy I have not admitted. Give me the freedom to celebrate what You give to others without measuring it against what You have given me. Amen.
